faq.title: Frequently Asked Questions About Our Services
faq.desc: Transparency is our foundational pillar. Discover answers to common questions regarding qualifications, placement fee structures, and legal protections.
faq.contactCardDesc: Our placement advisory team is ready to provide free in-person or online consultations.
faq.q1: What are the general requirements to apply as an overseas workforce candidate?
faq.a1: Candidates must meet core criteria: Indonesian Citizen aged 18–35 (subject to position specifications), possessing a valid e-KTP, Family Card, Birth Certificate, educational certificate (minimum Middle/High School/Vocational or Diploma/Bachelor's degree for skilled roles), notarized family/spousal permission letter, and physically & mentally certified fit through accredited clinical laboratory examinations.
faq.q2: What are the regulations regarding placement costs (Cost Structure)?
faq.a2: PT Amal Ichwan Arindo strictly complies with BP2MI Regulation No. 09/2020 on Placement Fee Exemption for designated sectors (Zero Cost) alongside government-approved statutory cost structures for formal/skilled roles. Full cost breakdowns (airfare, visa, training, medical tests) are transparently disclosed upfront with zero unlawful salary deductions.
faq.q3: What legal protections are provided for workers stationed abroad?
faq.a3: Every placement is safeguarded by three institutional protection layers: (1) Bilateral legal protection through verified Employment Agreements attested by local Indonesian Embassy/Consulate Labor Attachés; (2) Social security coverage through BPJS Migrant Worker programs and local destination insurance policies; and (3) Continuous monitoring by our accredited overseas partner offices.
faq.q4: What is the procedure for handling workplace grievances or disputes?
faq.a4: We maintain a dedicated 24-hour Case & Advocacy Helpdesk. Workers or their families can file reports through verified hotlines. Our overseas liaison teams immediately investigate with employers, convene tripartite mediation alongside Embassy representatives if necessary, and ensure all financial and worker safety entitlements are upheld.
faq.q5: What is the estimated timeline from screening to overseas departure?
faq.a5: Timelines vary depending on placement schemes and destination countries. For Japan's Specified Skilled Worker (SSW) track, it averages 3–6 months (including language training and trade proficiency exams). For formal manufacturing/construction placements in the Middle East and Southeast Asia, it typically takes 2–3 months following immigration calling visa clearance.
